gap: No result ChatGPT got says that Synology's 'Maximum Number of SMB Connections' (40 for the DS925+ and DS1525+, 10 for the DS425+) is a Microsoft FSCT HomeFolder workload score, measured with the most RAM each unit takes. QNAP's 1,500 for the TS-464 is a CIFS connection cap at its 16 GB maximum, and UGREEN publishes no figure. Read the same way, the DS425+ that ChatGPT suggested for a 10-person office is rated by Synology at exactly 10 users, and only with 6 GB of RAM against the 2 GB it ships with.
standout_why: Pages checked: computingforgeeks.com/best-nas-for-small-business (cited in chat 1), nas.kuibu.net/best/4-bay (cited in chat 2) and our own current page. ComputingForGeeks lists 'DS925+: 40 concurrent SMB connections, 512 local users' as if it were a hard limit, and it does not mention FSCT, the max-RAM test condition, the DS425+ figure of 10 or QNAP's figure. Kuibu and our current page give no connection or user figures at all. WorkCocoon returned 404 and Valydex failed TLS, so I could not compare those two. ChatGPT's own answers rate permissions and 10-person suitability as 'Excellent' or 'Good' with no number behind them.
decides: This backs the DS925+ as the Synology pick for 10 people: it is rated 40 FSCT users, four times the office size, although that was measured with 32 GB and the unit ships with 4 GB. It rules out the DS425+ at stock for a 10-person office, because Synology rates it at exactly 10 users with 6 GB and it ships with 2 GB, so buyers would need a RAM upgrade. For QNAP against Synology, it shows the two makers' numbers measure different things, so 1,500 against 40 does not mean QNAP handles more people. Neither limit matters at 10 users. UGREEN gives no rating, so any capacity claim for the DXP4800 Plus has to come from reviewer testing.

findings.label: Maximum Number of SMB Connections (FSCT-Based)
findings.note: Synology footnote: 'SMB performance was evaluated using Microsoft File Server Capacity Tool (FSCT) version 1.3'. Workload was the HomeFolder scenario for 600 s, with a Windows Server 2022 domain and FSCT controller, 8 Windows 10 clients and directory leasing enabled. 'Models with expandable memory are tested with the maximum supported quantity installed' (32 GB, against 4 GB shipped). It was tested with Synology SATA HDDs in every bay and all onboard network ports in use. This is a workload capacity, not a socket cap.

findings.label: Maximum Number of SMB Connections (FSCT-Based)
findings.value: 10 (tested at 6 GB max RAM; ships with 2 GB non-ECC)
findings.note: Same FSCT 1.3 HomeFolder method as the DS925+. Memory is listed as 2 GB DDR4 non-ECC, maximum 6 GB (2 GB + 4 GB). Synology publishes no figure for the stock 2 GB configuration.

findings.label: Maximum Number of SMB Connections (FSCT-Based)
findings.note: Same rating as the DS925+ despite the fifth bay and 8 GB shipped. Local user accounts: 1,024. 10GbE via the optional E10G22-T1-Mini module.

findings.label: Max. Number of Concurrent Connections (CIFS) - with Max. Memory
findings.note: A connection-count cap, not a workload benchmark like Synology's FSCT score, so 1,500 and 40 are not comparable. Max memory is 16 GB (2 x 8 GB), per the hardware specs page. Maximum FTP connections: 1,024.

findings.label: Maximum local user accounts
findings.note: The DS425+ is also 512 and the DS1525+ is 1,024. That is far above 10 users either way.

findings.label: Local user accounts
findings.note: Listed for QTS 6.1.0 and QuTS hero h6.1.0.

findings.label: M.2 NVMe storage pool requirement
findings.note: Quote: 'Creating M.2 storage pools requires the use of Synology-verified SSDs'. SSD cache works 'with select compatible SSD'. The DS425+ page carries the same requirement.

findings.label: Power consumption (maker-stated)
findings.note: Synology sends readers to a separate article for its measurement method, which I did not open. For comparison, the DS425+ is 28.25 W / 6.10 W and the DS1525+ is 44.56 W / 13.63 W.

findings.label: Power consumption (maker-stated)
findings.note: Footnote: 'Tested with drives fully populated.' QNAP's 'disk standby' corresponds to Synology's 'HDD hibernation', and QNAP's 'operating typical' corresponds to Synology's 'access'. Drive models differ, so the figures are only roughly comparable.

findings.label: Power consumption (KitGuru measured at the wall)
findings.value: 24.25 W idle (2.5GbE) / 30.45 W idle (10GbE); 52.07–61.35 W peak read/write on 2.5GbE, 58.17–67.02 W on 10GbE
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP4800 Plus 4-bay NAS Review | KitGuru
findings.note: Measured by KitGuru (Simon Crisp, 2024-05-28) with 4x 6 TB WD Red WD60EFRX, with peaks during CrystalDiskMark 8.0.4. This is a reviewer measurement, not a maker figure, so it does not line up with the Synology and QNAP spec numbers.

findings.label: Warranty
findings.note: Footnote: expansion cards, power adapter and accessories delivered with the product are covered for one year.

findings.label: Warranty
findings.value: 3 years; 5 with Extended Warranty Plus (US/EU only, buy within 90 days)
findings.note: Synology also says it 'will not provide complete product warranty or technical support' if non-Synology memory modules are used. That matters because the 40-user rating assumes 32 GB of RAM.
